I ran two searches (the instructions asked for one, so the second was an extra). Most sources are vendor-adjacent blogs or review sites, and their figures often disagree, so treat the numbers as rough.

- **Linear:** Several sources describe it as fast and keyboard-driven with opinionated defaults, which means less configuration but less flexibility. One reviewer says it hits a free-tier cap at 250 issues, then costs about $10/user/month on Basic. ([devtoolpicks](https://devtoolpicks.com/blog/best-linear-alternatives-indie-hackers-2026), [toolradar](https://toolradar.com/compare/jira-vs-linear))
- **Jira:** It's the enterprise default, with deep customization and a large marketplace. One source lists a free tier for up to 10 users, then about $7.75/user/month. ([tech-insider](https://tech-insider.org/?p=3664), [devtoolpicks](https://devtoolpicks.com/blog/best-linear-alternatives-indie-hackers-2026))
- **GitHub Issues:** It's free and works best for teams already living in GitHub. It's weaker on portfolio management and advanced reporting. ([airframe](https://www.airframe.ai/product/github-com-features-issues/compare))
- **Plane:** It's an open-source, AGPL-licensed tool positioned as a Linear and Jira alternative, with issues, cycles, modules, and roadmaps. The Community Edition is free to self-host, and cloud Pro is listed at $6/seat/month. Some reviewers note its documentation and community are smaller than Linear's. ([devtoolpicks](https://devtoolpicks.com/blog/best-linear-alternatives-indie-hackers-2026), [use-apify](https://use-apify.com/blog/linear-alternatives-2026))

**Discrepancies:** GitHub star counts for Plane range from about 39.7K to 52.5K across sources, and pricing tiers vary by source. Check current pricing and star counts directly before deciding.

**Bottom line:** Linear is generally the pick for speed and developer experience. Jira fits enterprises needing heavy customization. GitHub Issues suits GitHub-centric teams that want minimal tooling. Plane suits teams that want a Linear-like tool they can self-host.

Four sources cover this, with some caveats about bias.

- **Shortcut** is the closest swap if you want Linear's speed plus roadmap and docs without per-seat costs. If you want Linear's speed plus a roadmap and docs without the seat creep, Shortcut is the closest swap. Its integration library is thinner than Jira's or ClickUp's, and SSO and advanced analytics sit behind the $12 Business tier.
- **Plane** is the open-source option. One review says if finance demands you own your data, self-host Plane for free. A rework.com comparison table describes it as Linear-like in UX but a younger product with fewer integrations. I translated that from the German version of the page.
- **Jira and ClickUp** fit broader needs. Jira and ClickUp are only the answer if you've outgrown pure engineering and need to drag in PMs, ops, and clients.
- **Height** is positioned for smaller teams. One comparison table lists its ideal team size as 5-100, with CTOs and tech leads as the main buyers.
- **Pricing context:** One review notes that Linear's free plan caps you at 250 issues and 2 teams. Another source says paid plans start at $8 per user per month.

Caveats: the sources are mostly comparison blogs and vendor-adjacent content (one is from ONES, which sells a competing product), so their rankings are opinion, not independent benchmarks. The rework.com tables appear in several languages and differ slightly between versions. I did not check current prices, so verify those on each vendor's site.

Linear's main competitors are Jira, Shortcut, Plane, GitHub Issues, ClickUp and Height. Most of the sources below are vendor-adjacent review blogs, so treat the comparisons as opinion. Prices and star counts differ between sources, so check them on each vendor's site.

| Tool | Positioning vs Linear | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Jira** | Enterprise default, with deep customization and a large marketplace. | It's heavier to configure than Linear. Its free tier is reported at up to 10 users, then about $7.75/user/month. |
| **Shortcut** | Closest swap: Linear-style speed plus roadmaps and docs. | Its integration library is thinner than Jira's or ClickUp's. SSO and advanced analytics sit in the $12 Business tier. |
| **Plane** | Open-source (AGPL) option with a Linear-like UX. | You can self-host it free. Cloud Pro is listed at about $6/seat/month. It has fewer integrations and a smaller community. |
| **GitHub Issues** | Free and minimal, best for teams already working in GitHub. | It's weaker on portfolio management and reporting. |
| **ClickUp** | Broad work-management tool for teams that include PMs, ops and clients. | It's less focused on engineering than Linear. |
| **Height** | Aimed at smaller teams, with one table listing an ideal team size of 5–100. | I only found this in one comparison table. |

For reference, Linear is described as fast and keyboard-driven, with opinionated defaults that mean less configuration but less flexibility. Its free plan is reported to cap at 250 issues and 2 teams, with paid plans from about $8–10/user/month.
